name: bp-01-blueprint-schema
title: BP-01 — the blueprint as a versioned, backend-neutral artifact
claim: Stage 1 / BP-01 of the review program. The canonical blueprint is now a VERSIONED, backend-neutral artifact with a checked contract and a static validator -- the first of the three claims (blueprint fidelity) made a first-class, tested object rather than an implicit input. Specifically: (a) a `blueprint_version` field + versioned JSON schema; (b) a canonical/backend split (CompileOptions) so backend/run parameters (tension_scale, rules_seed) are kept OUT of the canonical biological state and recorded separately; (c) a static validator (`validate_blueprint` + `multicell-blueprint validate`) that reports structured diagnostics (errors AND contract warnings), not a success badge; (d) three hand-authored worked examples that validate and compile identically to BOTH backends.
experiment: Add `blueprint.canonical.{CompileOptions, split_canonical, canonical_violations}`, `Blueprint.canonical_state()`, `schema.validate_blueprint`, and a CLI `validate` command. Add `blueprint_version` to the schema and to the canonical blueprints, and strip the run parameter `rules_seed` from the committed Sego blueprint. Author three example blueprints (simple geometry, mixed populations, infection field). Assert the acceptance criteria as tests.
result: All BP-01 acceptance criteria pass (tests/test_blueprint_canonical.py, 9 tests): the same immutable canonical blueprint compiles to both backends; `canonical_state()` is identical regardless of backend/run parameters; the validator emits structured error/warning diagnostics; a missing blueprint_version and in-blueprint backend/run parameters are warnings (not errors). The committed Sego and mechanics-divergence blueprints are now versioned and validate contract-clean. 174 passed overall.

purpose.question: Can the biological blueprint be specified as a versioned, backend-neutral, statically-validated artifact, independent of CPM/vertex implementations?
purpose.mechanism: A canonical schema + a split that routes backend/run parameters to CompileOptions makes the biological state immutable across backends; a static validator turns each semantic invariant into a checked diagnostic.
purpose.expected_outcome: One canonical blueprint accepted unchanged by both backends; backend/run parameters recorded separately; validator reports problems explicitly.

key_assumptions: Backend/run parameters are currently tension_scale (vertex) and rules_seed (run); genuine model constants (const) remain canonical.
blueprint_version is optional for back-compat (a warning, not an error) but set on every canonical artifact going forward.
This is Stage 1: round-trip fidelity of AREA/footprint/contact/topology (BP-02) and physical initialization (BP-03) are the next steps, not claimed here.

baseline.name: canonical-blueprint
baseline.description: The Sego canonical blueprint is the worked artifact the schema/validator/compile contract is exercised against.

behavior_tests.name: same-canonical-blueprint-both-backends
behavior_tests.description: The same immutable canonical blueprint compiles to CPM and vertex.

behavior_tests.name: backend-run-params-not-canonical
behavior_tests.description: tension_scale and rules_seed are split out of the canonical blueprint and flagged by the validator.

behavior_tests.name: validator-structured-diagnostics
behavior_tests.description: validate_blueprint returns {severity, path, message} for errors and contract warnings.

controls.name: dirty-blueprint-negative
controls.description: A blueprint missing `domain` yields an ERROR diagnostic; a blueprint with tension_scale yields a WARNING — the validator exposes problems, not a badge.

limitations: BP-01 establishes the schema + contract + validator. It does NOT yet prove area/footprint/contact/adjacency/topology fidelity (BP-02) or physical constraint-satisfying initialization (BP-03).
The canonical split currently recognizes tension_scale/rules_seed/migration_scale; further backend/run keys are added as backends grow.

report.title: The blueprint is now a versioned, backend-neutral, validated artifact
report.verdict: BP-01 is complete: a versioned canonical schema, a canonical/backend split that keeps backend/run parameters out of the biological state (CompileOptions), a static validator with structured diagnostics (+ a `validate` CLI), and three worked examples that validate and compile identically to both backends. The committed Sego and mechanics-divergence blueprints are versioned and contract-clean. This makes Claim 1 (blueprint fidelity) a first-class, tested object and unblocks Stage 2 (round-trip / geometric fidelity).
report.main_insight: The biological specification can be stated once, versioned, and validated independently of either substrate; backend/run parameters are a separate, recorded concern.
report.caveat: Schema + contract + validator only; geometric round-trip fidelity (area, footprint, contact, topology) is BP-02, not claimed here.

findings.statement: One versioned canonical blueprint compiles unchanged to both backends; backend/run parameters are separated into CompileOptions and flagged by a static validator; three worked examples validate and compile on both backends.

evidence.observed: 9 BP-01 acceptance tests pass; sego + mechanics_divergence validate contract-clean; 174 passed overall

findings.explanation: A canonical schema + split + validator make the biological blueprint a first-class, tested artifact.
findings.next_action: Stage 2 / BP-02: prove round-trip geometric fidelity (area, footprint, contact, adjacency, topology) with explicit error measures.
